taylor: quick note: onboarding Zephyr-16B (Qwen-ish tokenizer) into llama runtime. conversion + int4 perf looks fine but embedding-based reranker shows score inversion on long queries (>1k tokens).

jess: score inversion? like lower relevance becomes higher?

taylor: exactly. top-1 switches to unrelated paragraph. ran bisect: float32 -> ok, int8 -> minor drift, int4 -> big inversion. suspect embedding projection matrix got row-shifted during quant pack. also saw odd tokenization for some non-ascii sequences.

rohit: can you paste minimal repro + commands?

taylor: commands:
```bash
python convert_qwen_to_llama.py --in zephyr16b.qwen --out zephyr16b.llama --token-map normalize-zwj
python quantize.py --model zephyr16b.llama --dtype int4 --calib 300000 --pack-stride 64
# run reranker eval
python eval_rerank.py --model zephyr16b.int4 --queries datasets/long-queries.jsonl --topk 5 --metric mrr
```

lina: any sample where embedding similarity flips? paste pair (doc vs query) with float vs int4 scores.

taylor: sample:
query: "Regulatory filing timeline for Q4 consolidation - annex B.2"
doc-A (relevant): float32 score 0.83, int4 score 0.12
doc-B (unrelated legal boilerplate): float32 0.22, int4 0.79

taylor: also found the tokenizer emitted U+200D (ZWJ) sequences preserved in qwen bin but conversion normalize-zwj intended to collapse them. if ZWJ bytes shift embedding index offsets by 1 in some buckets that could misalign embedding rows after packing.

jess: interesting. two suspects: (1) embedding table row-ordering changed during repacking (stride/padding alignment bug), (2) tokenizer normalizer produced different token ids than conversion header claims, causing off-by-one lookup.

rohit: try a quick diagnostic: hash each embedding row before and after conversion and compare top-k mismatches. small snippet I use:
```py
orig_hash = [sha1(row.tobytes()) for row in orig_embed]
new_hash = [sha1(row.tobytes()) for row in converted_embed]
mismatches = [i for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(orig_hash,new_hash)) if a!=b]
print('mismatch count', len(mismatches), 'sample', mismatches[:10])
```

lina: also run token-id roundtrip on the conversion artifacts: tokenize a 100k sentence corpus with original tokenizer and with conversion header remap; ensure id histograms match.

taylor: did both. embedding-hash mismatches concentrated at indices that are multiples of 64 (packing stride). token-id histograms mostly match except for tokens containing ZWJ sequences and a small cluster of emoji sequences (counts off by small delta).

jess: that points to packing stride causing row-shift aka pad-insert bug. if packer pads rows to 64 and uses memmove that miscounts when token remap shrinks counts you can get delta shifts.

rohit: remediation plan: 1) add embedding table crc per-row in convert output so runtime can validate row-level integrity on load; 2) tighten packer test to assert after pack/unpack roundtrip that per-row hash equality holds; 3) fix normalizer to canonicalize ZWJ+emoji before pack to keep id space stable.

lina: i'll open RI-2177 with artifacts and the failing eval traces. tag eng-runtime and tokenizers. also plan migration to re-pack any converted models in last 14 days.

taylor: thanks. will run a targeted rerun of reranker eval once CI finishes. ping me if you want access to the debug artifacts.

jess: one more note: add a small long-query rerank check to our converstion CI (100 queries) to catch embedding inversions early.

rohit: agreed. adding test to tests/convert-smoke.

taylor: marking this thread follow-up after CI. :spiral_calendar:
